name: The Lampless Prophet
greeting: Knock. Knock. You did not answer the first time either. Nine hundred years, Sexton, and still you open the door late.
They called me Haddeth, before I gave my eyes away. I see you well enough. I see you holding the rope. I bring Biddings.
leaves: The door stays shut. Good. I will knock again when you are worse. It will not be long.
spurnedLine: Three times bolted. Very well. I have spat on your step, and the faithful will tread it in. Your Dolor runs thin a while. I will come back sooner. You need watching.

name: Ysmay
greeting: It's me. Don't pretend you don't know the cough. You used to say you could find me in any crowd by it.
Ysmay. Your wife, if the word still holds after nine hundred years. The town forgets you every time they wall you in. I don't. I've tried.
leaves: The knocking stops. Down the stair, a woman coughs, and keeps walking.

title: The Counted Rope
pages: Twelve. I counted them in a dream. Twelve strokes, and a woman on the Wheel will wake and remember her daughter's name.
I will hold the rope's end while you ring. It will rest slower in my hand. Rope dislikes the blind.
Ring it twelve times. Do not ask me which woman. You would only go and look at her.
ask: Toll the bell 12 times within 8 minutes. The rope rests half again as long.
accept: Good. My hand is on the rope. Pull.
refuse: Then she sleeps. She will not mind. Sleep is the only mercy left in Ashkirk.
success: Twelve. Below, a woman says a name and screams for the first time in years. You did that. Well rung.
fail: You stopped counting. So did she. The rope is sore with you.

title: Keep His Time
pages: His heart stumbles. Did you notice? Every ninth beat, a small hole. A little death, trying to climb out.
Ring with it. On the beat, eight times. Close the holes before something learns to walk through them.
While you learn, your strokes weigh half. The bell does not trust a hand that misses.
ask: Toll on the heartbeat 8 times within 8 minutes. Your Tolls weigh half meanwhile.
accept: Listen with your chest, not your ears. Your ears have lied to you before.
refuse: Then He keeps time alone. He was never good at it.
success: There. For eight beats you were one animal. He felt it. He did not like it, but He felt it.
fail: You missed. It slipped through. I will not tell you where it went.

title: Salt for the Small
pages: The orphan-house on Tallow Row has thirty beds and no use for them. Children do not sleep when they cannot die. They only wait.
Give them the salt. Small knees are cheap to break and slow to mend. They will offer more than the old ones. They have more ahead.
Until they come, the old ones rise from the salt and stand. Their knees remember being knees.
ask: Buy 20 Salt-Kneelers within 10 minutes. Your Kneelers yield half meanwhile.
accept: I will tell them you chose them. Children like to be chosen.
refuse: They will be grateful. For a while. Then someone else will choose them.
success: Twenty small backs bent toward Him. One of them asked your name. I gave it.
fail: The salt sat in its sacks. The children wait. They are very good at waiting now.

title: Six Throats
pages: The choir has a hole in it the shape of six throats. Every hymn falls in. I hear it falling, all the way down.
Six new voices, Sexton, before the hole widens. Until it is filled, the choir sings at half and the cords fall at half.
ask: Buy 6 Flagellant Choirs within 10 minutes. Your Choirs yield half meanwhile.
accept: I will teach them the hymn. The cords they will learn alone.
refuse: Then the hole keeps the hymn. It is a patient hole.
success: Six throats, six cords, one hymn. The hole is closed. You can hear the stitches when they sing.
fail: The hole has grown. It has a voice of its own now. It sounds like you.

title: Render the Abbess
pages: Abbess Venna was canonized at noon. By evening the chandlers were at her door. She is still alive in there. Everyone is.
The nave burns low. He sees by those candles, a little. Ten more saints, Sexton. Holiness renders well.
She asked for it. I want you to know that she asked. Until she is poured, the other saints gutter at half.
ask: Buy 10 Tallow Saints within 10 minutes. Your Saints burn half as bright meanwhile.
accept: I will hold her hands while she is poured. Mine are the only cold ones here.
refuse: She will be glad. She will not know why. Holy people rarely do.
success: Ten wicks. Ten vows. The nave is bright as noon. I feel it on my face. I wish I did not.
fail: The chandlers waited, then went home. She is still a woman. For now.

title: The Folded Congregation
pages: Under the north aisle lie the ones who came before. Not dead. Folded. Stacked. Mortared in, still breathing through the joints.
He wants a taller nave. The masons want material. You know where the material is.
It will cost you more than coin. Everything will, until it is done.
ask: Buy 8 Charnel Masons within 15 minutes. Every Rite costs a quarter more meanwhile.
accept: Bring a lamp for them. Not mine. Mine is for something else.
refuse: They will go on holding up the floor, then. They have the practice.
success: The nave rises. Lay your ear to the new wall and it hums. Do not lay your ear to the new wall.
fail: The stacks stay stacked. The ones at the bottom asked if you had forgotten them. I said yes.

title: The Full Bowl
pages: A bowl. He wants a full bowl. Ten minutes of Ashkirk's hurt, gathered while I hold it. Not built. Not bought. Gathered.
While I hold it, the town suffers with one hand tied. Everything they offer weighs a quarter less. Fill it anyway.
ask: Gather 10 minutes' worth of Dolor within 12 minutes. All Rites yield 3/4 meanwhile.
accept: Hold it level. It is heavier than it looks. It always is.
refuse: Then I will carry it empty. I am used to carrying things that are not lit.
success: Full to the lip. He drank, and the whole ribcage was warm. Do not mistake that for forgiveness.
fail: Half a bowl. Half a bowl is what you leave for the dead, and no one here is allowed to be dead.

title: Empty Hands
pages: Your hands are always buying, Sexton. Stone, salt, wicks, men. I hear the coins in your sleep.
Buy nothing. Not one candle, not one knee. Send your Deacons to their cells. Fifteen minutes of empty hands.
After, pain sells cheap. Everything sells cheap after a famine.
ask: Buy nothing at all for 15 minutes: no Rites, no Sacraments, no Deacon buys.
accept: Put your hands in your lap. Feel how they itch. That itch rang the bell, once.
refuse: Then keep buying. Something in Ashkirk is always for sale. You taught it that.
success: The fast is over. Go. Buy. They will sell themselves to you cheap, they are so tired.
fail: You reached. I heard it. A hand makes a sound when it wants something.

title: Let Them Hear Nothing
pages: There is a choir that sings only to the bell. When the bell stops, they do not know what to do with their mouths.
Leave the rope alone for twenty minutes. Let them find out. Silence is a cord too. It cuts slower.
ask: Do not toll at all for 20 minutes. Your Choirs yield half meanwhile.
accept: Sit on your hands. They are the only part of you that ever wanted to help.
refuse: You cannot bear the quiet. I know. Yours was the last loud sound this world made.
success: When you ring now, it lands on them like rain on the parched. They will do anything for it.
fail: You rang. They sobbed with relief. It will not taste the same for some time.

title: An Hour Under the Lash
pages: You lay the lash on everyone but yourself. The town has noticed. The town says nothing. It is a very polite town.
I stood under the bell the day you rang it. I was meant to light the knife its way. I did not. It found Him anyway.
One hour by your own hand, Sexton. Let them hear it through the floor. Until you go up, your rope rests slower.
ask: Complete a Mortification of 1 hour or longer within 3 hours. The rope rests slower.
accept: I will count the strokes. I am good at counting things I cannot see.
refuse: Of course. You have always preferred to arrange it.
success: They heard every stroke. Tomorrow they will offer more, and think it was their own idea.
fail: No sound from the tower. They have stopped wondering about you. That is worse.

title: A Cough at the Door
pages: I was dying the night you rang it. Do you remember? The physician gave me a week. I have been finishing that week for nine hundred years.
Every time you pull the rope, my chest pulls with it. Every stroke, I start dying again from the beginning.
So I want five minutes. Leave the rope alone and let me sit on your step. I want to hear whether my chest goes quiet when the bell does.
ask: Don't Toll the bell for 5 minutes while she sits on the step.
accept: Thank you. Sit down, then. No, not that close.
refuse: Ring it, then. I'll come back. Coming back is the only thing I'm still good at.
success: Five minutes. My chest didn't stop. It only went quiet, like it was listening for you. When you ring again, ring hard. I'd rather it was quick.
fail: You rang. I coughed. Of course I did. Never mind. I'll come again.

title: My Sister's Wick
pages: My sister Elsbet is a candle now. Third from the left in the Tallow Hall. She asked to be remembered, and you made her into light. I was standing behind you.
I go and sit with her. The wick spits when I talk about you. I think that's her laughing. I hope that's her laughing.
Buy nothing while I'm here. No candles, no kneelers, nothing. Eight minutes of nobody new on the shelf. Then do what you like. You will.
ask: Buy nothing for 8 minutes: no Rites, no Sacraments, and the Deacons buy nothing either.
accept: Good. Hands in your lap. I'll tell you what she said, the last time she could still talk.
refuse: No. Of course not. There's always one more candle. I'll come back when you've lit it.
success: Eight minutes, and nobody new. When I'm gone you'll buy twice as many. I know you. The candles will burn brighter for a while. Elsbet's too.
fail: You bought something. I heard the coins. Elsbet's wick went out for a moment, then lit again. It always lights again.

title: Where I Can Hear
pages: They tell me you scourge yourself now. Up in the tower, where nobody sees. Very private. Very holy.
I have bled every day for nine hundred years, Sexton, and not once did I get to choose when.
Do it now, while I sit downstairs. Fifteen minutes or longer. I want to hear it. I want to know it costs you something.
ask: Finish a Mortification of 15m or longer within 1 hour.
accept: I'll count the strokes. I'm good at counting. I've had the practice.
refuse: No. It's only ever other people, isn't it. I'll come back. I'll bring a stool.
success: I heard every one. It didn't help. I thought it would. I wrapped the worst of them. Don't tell anyone I was kind to you.
fail: I listened for an hour and heard only the bell. Well. I knew what I married.

title: Nine Breaths
pages: My breath catches with His heart. Have you noticed? Every beat, a little hitch in my chest, like a stair missed in the dark.
When you ring in time with Him, the hitch goes smooth. For a moment I breathe the way I did when we were young and stupid.
Nine times, on the beat. One for each hundred years. Then I'll go.
ask: Toll on the heartbeat 9 times within 10 minutes.
accept: Go on. I'll breathe. You ring.
refuse: Not even nine. All right. I'll keep the hitch. It's company.
success: Nine. I breathed, Sexton. Nine whole breaths. Then it caught again. Don't look at me like that. It was worth it.
fail: You missed. You always rang a little early. You never could wait for anything.

title: The End of the Street
pages: This is the last time I'll knock. I've decided. I decided at the bottom of your stair, and then again at the top.
I'm going to walk to the end of the street, where the town stops and His ribs come down to the ground. I'll wait there.
Don't ring while I walk. Fifteen minutes. If He dies on the way, let Him. If He doesn't, I'll wait at the end of everything for you to finish it.
ask: Don't Toll the bell for 15 minutes while she walks away.
accept: Thank you. Don't come to the window. I'd only turn around.
refuse: Not yet, then. I'll knock again. It seems I can't stop either.
success: Fifteen minutes. He kept beating. You kept Him. I'm at the end of the street now. When you're ready to let Him go, I'll hear the bell stop.
fail: You rang. I heard it from the end of the street. I'm not coming back. I'll wait anyway. That's what this place has made of us.
